mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous year's average for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST is below its 12-month average for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months, combined with falling industrial production (INDPRO), signals deteriorating labor and output conditions, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO < previous year's average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both UNRATE > 4.5% for three months and INDPRO is below its 12-month average for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during any period where INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which rapidly increases borrowing costs and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.75% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS < previous month - 100,000
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >100,000 in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, coupled with a decline in consumer spending (proxied by GDPC1), indicates households are saving more and spending less, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month average for 3 months AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0 for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when RSAFS is above its 12-month average for three months and GDPC1 is declining for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for six consecutive months signals a robust supply expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during any six-month period of consecutive INDPRO increases.
